ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, point $E$ is a point on the diagonal $BD$ of the square $ABCD$, $EF\perp BC$, $EG\perp CD$, with the feet of the perpendiculars being $F$ and $G$, respectively. If $CG=6$ and $CF=8$, what is the length of $AE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect CE, as shown in the diagram: \\
$\because$ Quadrilateral ABCD is a square, \\
$\therefore AD=CD$, $\angle ADE=\angle CDE$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, \\
In $\triangle ADE$ and $\triangle CDE$, \\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
AD=CD\\
\angle ADE=\angle CDE\\
DE=DE
\end{array}\right.$\\
$\therefore \triangle ADE\cong \triangle CDE$, \\
$\therefore AE=CE$, \\
$\because$ EF$\perp$BC, EG$\perp$CD, \\
$\therefore \angle EGC=\angle EFC=\angle C=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral EFCG is a rectangle, \\
$\therefore$ EF=CG, \\
$\because CG=6$, $CF=8$, \\
$\therefore AE=CE=\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=\boxed{10}$.
